content.thinking:
I'm working out the postmortem from the key facts: the reconciliation alert shows 240 of 240 shopper totals are off, the widest gap is {A3}, and the oldest affected purchase is at {A4}. The P2 deploy of 26f1d7e lines up with the diff showing record_purchase stopped updating total_this_month_cents. I'm now checking the running code, where record_purchase is doing something I still need to confirm.

I've confirmed that both record paths stopped updating the monthly total, so the drop is visible in the code that actually ran, not just in the diff. I'm now checking what shoppers would have seen on their statements.

I'm settling on how the symptom should read: shopper monthly totals fell short of the purchases behind them, and I'm listing the causal chain, starting with that symptom and then the reason purchases stopped moving the monthly total.

I'm settling on the root cause now: the change stopped keeping total_this_month_cents current on the assumption it could be derived from purchase history, but the field stayed on the account and the statement, spend summary and reconciliation check all still read the stored figure rather than summing purchases.

I'm checking whether the P1 deploy can be ruled out as the cause, since the alert dates the oldest affected purchase at 04:00:00 on Nov 4, which falls after the P2 deploy at 03:59:32, so the first harm came after that later change.

I'm ruling out the P1 deploy: the alert dates the oldest affected purchase after the P2 change, so the first harm came later. I'm also ruling out a flag change, since no flags changed in the hour before onset apart from Argus's own.

I'm now moving on to the contributing factors: the spend-integrity check only runs every few days, so the drift went unnoticed for that long, and no test before the deploy checked that record_purchase kept the monthly total in step with purchases.

I'm now listing the contributing factors: the spend-integrity check only runs every few days, which let the drift go unnoticed, and no test I've seen checks that record_purchase keeps the monthly total in step with purchases, so I'm proposing a CI test that writes purchases through every path and asserts the reconciliation reports nothing.

I'm going over why nobody was paged: the alert linked no on-call incident, so a person was never told to roll back at alert time. I'm also noting the deriving path drops the month total too, which is a latent fault and still at risk, and that F1's fix covers only the deriving path on main while main's record_purchase still moves the total.

I'm checking the rollback side now: the deriving function was not touched by 26f1d7e, so it would still be present after reverting to 4c810f2, and it also drops the month total when that flag is on. The fix on main covers only that path, so the rollback would leave a live fault in place. I'm also listing the repair script as the first action item for the wrong totals.

I'm now drafting the action items: first a repair of the wrong monthly totals, then a shorter spend-integrity check interval, then paging on-call when the reconciliation alert fires, and I'm starting a CI test that writes purchases through every ledger path.

I'm now listing a contributing factor on the review side: the change stopped writing the stored total without moving the code that reads it to derive it, and I haven't seen any review step that checks a removed write against the field's readers.

I'm weighing whether the spend-integrity check interval and the missing pre-deploy test belong as contributing factors, and I'm checking the wording of the still-at-risk section against the facts. I'm also noting that the went-well list is starting to cover how Argus used the flag history to rule out a flag change.

I'm now reviewing the went-well and went-wrong sections: Argus read the flag provider's history, and the Investigator read the diff that tied the change to the symptom. Argus also held off acting on the recommendation, since nothing would confirm within its wait, and left the rollback to a person. Code-Fix proposed a draft PR with a repair script, and I'm noting that I should name it without describing what it does.

I'm noting that the paging gap belongs under what went wrong rather than as a contributing factor, since the alert linked no on-call incident and a person was never told to roll back when it fired. I also need to record that Code-Fix's patch covers only the deriving path on main and leaves the record_purchase path of the running revision untouched.

I'm leaving the paging gap under what went wrong, since the alert linked no on-call incident and nobody was told to roll back when it fired. I'm also checking that the rollback target still carries the month-total path, which the removed lines in the diff suggest it does.

I'm settling on the rollback piece now: reverting to the earlier revision puts back the record_purchase write, but the deriving path would still drop the month total, so an action item needs to cover the fix on main. The root cause and the rollback reach are both settled from the diff, with nothing left unverified there.

I'm noting the timing step: the row that read the state fixes what was known at that moment, and the replicas all ran 26f1d7e as of that row, so the change can be dated by the P2 deploy. For the causal chain, I'm tying the first step to the alert, the second to the code and the spend-integrity comparison, the third to the deploy, the diff and the replica check, and the fourth to the diff, the code, and the comparison steps that show the write was dropped.

I'm checking the timing and ruling out the other causes: the alert puts the oldest affected purchase after the P2 deploy, and the flag history rules out a flag change. The spend-integrity check runs every few days, so that interval is what I need to keep in mind for the write-up.

action_items.item: Export the accounts and run Code-Fix's repair script against them (scripts/repair_monthly_totals.py), first as a dry run and then with --apply, and load the corrected accounts back. Do this once a revision that maintains the month total is running, and before the month rolls over.
Run the spend-integrity check that compares stored monthly totals with the purchases far more often than it runs now.

Add a test that runs for every change to the purchase ledger. It should record purchases through each write path (record_purchase, record_purchase_deriving_the_month and record_a_purchase both ways) and assert that reconcile_monthly_totals reports nothing for the result.
Route SpendTotalsDoNotReconcile to the on-call rotation so that a person is paged when it fires.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' stored monthly spend totals no longer matched the purchases behind them: each affected total came out short of what the shopper had bought this month.

Purchases recorded on the running code were added to the account and to the lifetime total, but the stored this-month total was left where it was. The reconciliation check compares that stored figure with the sum of the in-month purchases, so it found the stored figure short.

ruled_out.what: The earlier deploy of revision 4c810f2 at {P1.1}: the alert dates the oldest affected purchase at {A4}, which is after the later deploy at {P2.1}.
A feature-flag change: the flag provider's history showed {T14.2} flag changes by anyone but Argus in the window before the onset.

causal_chain.step: Revision 26f1d7e, deployed at {P2.1}, removed the update to total_this_month_cents from record_purchase. As of {T11.1}, all {T11.2} replicas were running that revision.
The change stopped keeping the month total on the reasoning that it could be derived from the history, but the code that uses it still reads the stored field instead of deriving it.

input.cause_in_plain_words: A code change to the shop stopped updating each shopper's saved running total for the current month when a purchase was recorded, but the shop's statements and checks still read that saved total, so it fell further behind what shoppers had actually bought.

contributing_factors.factor: The only thing that found the drift was the spend-integrity check, which runs once every {A5} days. No more frequent check was seen comparing stored monthly totals with the purchases behind them.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A check that ran more often would have caught the wrong totals soon after the deploy, so far fewer totals would have been written wrong before anyone knew.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: Before revision 26f1d7e was deployed, no check was seen that records purchases through the ledger's write paths and confirms the stored monthly total still matches the purchases.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Such a check would have failed on a change that stopped moving the month total, and the change would have been held back before it reached production.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent read the deployment's diff, which showed the month-total update removed from record_purchase.
Argus read the flag provider's history and found no flag changes by anyone else before the onset, which ruled out a flag change.
Argus declined to roll back on its own, because nothing would show inside its wait whether the rollback worked. It left the rollback to a person as a recommendation instead.
The Code-Fix Agent proposed a draft pull request, #554, along with a one-off repair script for the totals already written wrong.

went_wrong: The alert paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it, so the rollback Argus recommended waited on a person noticing it.

input.root_cause: Revision 26f1d7e removed the line in record_purchase that added each in-month purchase's price to the account's stored total_this_month_cents, on the reasoning that the month could be derived from the purchase history. The field stayed on the account, though, and the monthly statement, the spend summary and the reconciliation check still read the stored figure rather than summing the purchases. From then on, every recorded purchase left the stored month total further behind the purchases.
input.still_at_risk: Every purchase recorded through either write path on the running revision could keep leaving shoppers' stored monthly totals short, and the totals already written wrong stay wrong in the monthly statements and spend figures that read them until someone rewrites them.
input.symptom: Shoppers' monthly spend totals fell short of the purchases behind them
